# Agent operations

Tool authorization and narrowing, system crons, environment configuration, and baked marketplaces for deployed agents. See [agent.md](./agent.md) for the platform architecture, [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md) for the control plane that stores this configuration, and [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md) for the process that applies it.

## Tool management and narrowing

The runtime uses a two-tier tool authorization model: **floor tools** (unconditional, always present) and **allowed tools** (database-driven, configurable per agent).

### Floor tools

Every Claude session the agent spawns includes a fixed set of seven **floor tools** (the `FLOOR_TOOLS` constant in `runtime/claude.ts`):

- `Read`: read-only file access
- `Write`: create files
- `Edit`: modify existing file content
- `Glob`: pattern-based file discovery
- `Grep`: content search
- `TodoWrite`: task tracking
- `Skill`: invoke skills

These are **non-revocable**: they do not come from the `AgentTool` table and are granted regardless of agent configuration. They give no meaningful capability beyond `Read` plus local edits, and they keep an agent useful when its tool configuration is empty. How a specialty manifest relates to them is covered in [specialties.md](./specialties.md#floor_tools-are-outside-manifest-authority).

`Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Agent` and `Monitor` are **not** in the floor set. They allow arbitrary command execution, external HTTP, sub-agent spawning and streaming monitors, so they must be present as enabled `AgentTool` rows to be available. An agent with no enabled `AgentTool` rows (or a 404 from the config endpoint) gets only the seven floor tools: no shell, no external fetches, no sub-agents.

### Configurable allowed tools (`AgentTool` table)

Tools beyond the floor set live in the `AgentTool` table (`admin/prisma/schema/schema.prisma`): one row per `pattern` per agent, unique on `(agentId, pattern)`, with an `enabled` flag. Creating an agent, through either the admin UI form (`POST /admin/agents`) or the JSON API (`POST /agents`), seeds `AgentTool` rows from the `tools[]` list of the agent's resolved specialty manifest. The bundled `specialist` type seeds `Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch` and `Agent` (see [agent-types.md](./agent-types.md#the-specialist-type)). Operators and integrations can then add, toggle and remove rows from the agent detail page or through `/agents/:id/tools` (see [agent-api-resources.md](./agent-api-resources.md#tools-allowed-tools-list)).

`GET /agents/:id/config` returns the patterns of the agent's **enabled** rows as `allowedTools`. The runtime fetches the bundle again every 60 seconds, stores the list in `AGENT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` and updates the live Claude config, and `claude.ts` merges it with `FLOOR_TOOLS` when it builds `--allowedTools`. Duplicates are dropped with floor tools first, so the floor always wins.

Tool changes flow like this:

1. An operator or integration changes `AgentTool` rows through the admin UI or `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /agents/:id/tools[/:toolId]`.
2. The agent's next 60-second config sync picks up the new `allowedTools`.
3. The next Claude session sees the new list. No pod restart is needed.

### Example: narrowing an agent to read-only mode

The `:toolId` path parameter is the `AgentTool` row's cuid primary key, not the tool's `pattern`, so look up the row ids first:

1. `GET /agents/:id/tools` and note the `id` of the rows whose `pattern` is `"Bash"`, `"WebSearch"` and `"WebFetch"`.
2. `DELETE /agents/:id/tools/:toolId` for each of those ids. To keep the row but switch it off, send `PATCH /agents/:id/tools/:toolId` with `{ "enabled": false }` instead.

After the next config sync Claude has no shell or external HTTP; only the seven floor tools remain, so the agent can still read, search and edit local files and invoke skills.

## System crons

A new agent's system crons come from its **specialty manifest**: the `crons` array of `<specialties dir>/<typeName>/manifest.yaml`. See [specialties.md](./specialties.md#crons) for the field reference and [agent-types.md](./agent-types.md#resolution-at-runtime) for how `typeName` is resolved (including the fallback to the default type for an unknown name). The `specialist` type shipped in this repo declares no crons.

On startup the runtime calls `POST /agents/:id/crons/reconcile` (`reconcileSystemCrons`, best effort and non-fatal; see [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md#boot-order-bootts)). Reconciliation runs in one transaction with three passes:

1. **Create or update.** Each manifest cron is matched by name. Existing rows keep their id (so run history survives) and their `enabled` state, and get the manifest's `schedule`, `prompt`, `silent` and `preCheck`. Missing rows are created with `system: true` and the manifest's `enabled` value.
2. **Link parents.** `parentCronId` is set from each entry's `parentCron`, and cleared back to `null` when an entry no longer declares a resolvable parent, so the link heals in both directions on every boot.
3. **Delete orphans.** System crons whose name is no longer in the manifest are deleted.

System crons reject changes to `schedule`, `prompt` and `preCheck` (403) and cannot be deleted; an `enabled`-only `PATCH` is allowed, so operators can still switch them on and off. See [agent-api-ops.md](./agent-api-ops.md#cron-jobs).

When a cron fires, `runtime/cron-handler.ts` handles it as described in [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md#entry-points-that-call-claude). Two job fields matter for operations:

- `silent`: the job needs no Slack channel or user, and `[silent]` replies are not posted. A non-silent job with neither `channel` nor `user` fails validation with a 422.
- `preCheck`: a script that runs before Claude from the workspace directory with the live process environment. A path starting with `./`, `../` or `/` is run directly; a `plugin:script` value resolves to that script in the installed plugin's `scripts/` directory. The script's trimmed stdout **replaces the prompt**. Exit code 0 with output runs the job; exit 0 with no output, or any exit code 1, skips the tick (recorded as `preCheck:no-output`); an exit code of 2 or higher is treated as a crash (`preCheck:crash`, with an alert posted when an alerts channel is configured); an unresolvable script is skipped as `preCheck:not-found`. A cron with a `preCheck` therefore only spends a Claude turn when there is real work.

Coding-specific crons (the loop and pipeline crons, patrol crons, and their prechecks) are documented in the [shipwright repository](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/agent-ops.md).

## Environment

The table lists the variables an operator sets for the admin service and the agent container. [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md#configuration) groups the admin variables by area and [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md#configuration) covers runtime tuning; the full agent runtime reference is [configuration-agent.md](./configuration-agent.md).

| Variable | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN` | admin | Dedicated Postgres datasource for the admin service (for example `postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db`). If unset, boot skips migrations with a log line. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ID` | entrypoint | The agent's id on the platform. Also settable with `--agent-id`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_API_URL` | entrypoint | Base URL of the admin API the entrypoint uses to fetch the agent's config at startup. Also settable with `--api-url`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_API_KEY` | entrypoint | Bearer token for the config fetch (`/agents/:id/config` and `/agents/:id/crons`). Also settable with `--api-key`. It must be a token the admin accepts for this agent (a per-agent DB token, or an entry in `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS` with scope `<agentId>` or `*`); anything else gets a 401 at startup. |
| `AGENT_HOME` | entrypoint | Persistent storage root. The server (`boot.ts`) defaults to `/data/agent-home`, which is also where the admin-generated Deployment mounts the agent's volume (`AGENT_HOME_MOUNT_PATH` in `admin/src/agent-manifest.ts`). Without it the entrypoint falls back to `~/.shipwright-agent`. Keep a volume here so mise caches, workspace files and `~/.claude` survive pod restarts. |
| `PORT` | admin | Port for the admin service (`admin/src/main.ts`). Default `3000`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_HEALTH_PORT` | agent | Port of the agent's single health server, used by Kubernetes probes. Default `3459`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_SESSION_SECRET` | admin | Secret that signs and verifies the `admin_session` JWT cookie. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_API_KEYS` | admin | Comma-separated `name:token:scope` tuples for env-based bearer auth on `/agents/*`. Scope is `*` (admin), an agent id (restricted to that agent), `platform.read` or `platform.ops`; see [agent-api.md](./agent-api.md). Optional: when absent only DB tokens and session cookies are accepted. |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | admin UI | Google OAuth 2.0 credentials for the login flow (optional when Okta is used). |
| `OKTA_ISSUER`, `OKTA_CLIENT_ID`, `OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET` | admin UI | Okta OIDC credentials. Okta login is enabled only when `OKTA_ISSUER` is set; Google login is unaffected either way. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS` | admin UI | Comma-separated emails allowed to log in with Google or Okta. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_APP_BASE_URL` | admin UI | Public base URL of the admin service, used to build the OAuth/OIDC redirect URIs and to decide whether the PWA tags are emitted (see [agent-web-ui.md](./agent-web-ui.md#pwa-shell)). Defaults to `http://localhost:{PORT}`. |
| `SHIPWRIGHT_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | secrets at rest | 64-character hex key (32 bytes) for AES-256-GCM. **If unset, secrets are stored in plain text**; set it in any real deployment. |
| `GH_APP_ID`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | GitHub App auth | GitHub App id and PEM private key (newlines may be `\n`-escaped). Required for the App auth path. |
| `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` | GitHub App auth | Optional pin of an installation that is always used. Without it the agent discovers the App's installations; see [github-multi-org.md](./github-multi-org.md). |
| `GH_APP_SLUG`, `GH_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `GH_APP_CLIENT_SECRET` | GitHub App auth | Persisted by the admin UI's App manifest flow (`github-provisioning-service.ts`) so the install link and OAuth settings can be rebuilt later. |
| `GH_TOKEN` | GitHub PAT auth | Personal access token for the `gh auth setup-git` path, used only when the App variables are absent. |
| `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH` | dev only | `"true"` enables `GET /admin/dev-login`. Always off when `NODE_ENV=production` (`dev-auth-guard.ts`). |

## Baked marketplaces (derived images)

A derived Docker image can ship extra Claude Code plugin marketplaces that the agent registers at boot, with no env var or database entry. Marketplace availability is an **image property**; which plugins an agent installs stays in the `AgentPlugin` table.

**Convention root:** `/opt/shipwright/marketplaces/` (`BAKED_MARKETPLACES_ROOT` in `runtime/setup.ts`).

Put one subdirectory per marketplace under it. Each must contain `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (the standard marketplace manifest). `installPlugins()` runs `claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` for every discovered directory **before** it registers the built-in marketplace, so plugins from a derived image resolve first.

```
/opt/shipwright/marketplaces/
  my-org-plugins/
    .claude-plugin/
      marketplace.json   <- required; triggers discovery
    plugins/
      ...
```

Directories without `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` are skipped silently, and a missing root yields no marketplaces. Registration is idempotent and non-fatal: a non-zero exit from `claude` is logged as a warning and startup continues. This path is part of the base-image contract that `runtime/Dockerfile` and `runtime/base-image-contract.smoke.test.ts` pin; change them together.
